transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I just keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. I work in retail, and recently I completely yelled at one of my employees just for putting stock on the wrong shelf. Afterward, I was actually shaking, because... well, that is just not how I usually treat people. I don't know what's going on with me, but I need to figure it out.
Have you been feeling irritable most of the time lately?

Yeah, definitely. Like I was just saying, it feels like I'm constantly blowing up over absolutely nothing. So, yes, I've been irritable pretty much all the time lately. That's why that incident with my employee and the shelves bothered me so much... I just snap, and it's really out of character for me.
Have you always been this way, or is this irritability a recent change for you?

No, not at all. It's a very recent change. This has really only been going on for about two weeks. It started right after we had a kitchen fire... it was during our first weekend working on the house. Ever since then, I've just been like this.
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Anxious? I mean, I guess I haven't really thought about it like that. I just know I've been on edge and snapping at people, like I said. But as for just feeling anxious... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed feeling that way specifically.
Do you feel anxious?

Like I was just saying, I don't really think so. I mean, I know I'm really wound up and irritable right now, but I wouldn't really use the word anxious. I just haven't noticed feeling that specific way, as far as I can tell.
Have you been avoiding certain people, places, or activities since the kitchen fire?

Yeah, I have. I've been avoiding the house completely. I also haven't touched our mortgage folder, and... well, even the herbs on my patio. Basically, anything that's tied to that day makes my chest tighten up, and I just can't make myself go near any of it.
Are there any other activities or places you've been avoiding since the kitchen fire besides the house and the things related to it that you mentioned?

No, not really. I mean, it's mostly just the house and everything connected to it, like I said. I go to work at the store, I go to the grocery store... I don't think I'm avoiding anything else, just the things that remind me of what happened.
Do you avoid the house because you're afraid of something happening again or because it reminds you of the fire?

It's really because it reminds me of it. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's just that anything tied to that day... the house, the mortgage folder, even the herbs on the patio... it just makes my chest tighten up. It's the reminders of what happened that I can't handle. I just can't bring myself to go near any of it.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself, or like things aren't real?

Yeah, I actually do. Sometimes when I'm at work, just walking through the store... it feels like I'm watching myself from a few feet away. It's hard to explain, but it's like the aisles and the customers are there, but they aren't quite real. I just feel like I'm moving through them on automatic.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the kitchen fire as if it were happening again?

Yeah, I do. It just... it keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. I could be doing something completely normal, like picking up a pan to wash it, or just opening up a spreadsheet at work, and suddenly it's like I'm right back there. I can smell the smoke, and I see the kitchen just filling up with it, and it happens before I can even stop it. It feels like it's happening all over again.
